citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
basis: The inn accepts about 1,050 card transactions a year as a sub-merchant of a payment facilitator. The sub-merchant agreement requires PCI DSS compliance and annual validation by self-assessment questionnaire. PCI SSC sets no size exemption; card-brand merchant levels were not verified, and the facilitator decides how the inn validates. Which SAQ fits is decided channel by channel in P03

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: The inn is a for-profit business (15 U.S.C. 44). It holds guest personal information and card data, publishes a privacy statement that speaks about card details, and quotes prices. No size threshold

obligation: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees
basis: A covered good or service includes short-term lodging at an inn, and a business includes an individual (464.1). The inn charges a mandatory $15 per-stay housekeeping fee and displays and quotes nightly rates on its website, by phone, in the booking engine and through the AI chat assistant. Analyzed with N72-R02

The rule covers consumer report information. The inn has no employees, runs no background checks or tenant screening, and obtains no consumer reports; the cleaners are employed by the cleaning service

obligation: State breach notification laws (Florida and other states)
basis: A covered entity under Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(b) expressly includes a sole proprietorship. The inn holds personal information of Florida residents (about 55% of guests), including names with driver license and passport images and card numbers, and of residents of other states. 501.171(2) and (8) (reasonable measures and disposal) are analyzed in P03; notice duties in P08

A bed and breakfast inn is a transient public lodging establishment (Fla. Stat. 509.242(1)(f)). Its operator must keep a chronological guest register with dates of occupancy and rates; registers more than 2 years old need not be made available

obligation: Florida unconscionable prices during a declared state of emergency
basis: The statute does not name hotels or inns. The inn rents rooms that evacuees may seek during a declared emergency, and its AI add-on changes nightly rates automatically with no ceiling, so the cautious reading is applied
The inn has no Illinois operations and collects no biometric identifiers; door access uses keypad codes and the inn has no employees or time clock

Not a final rule. Under the proposed size test (226.2(a)) an entity is covered only if it exceeds the SBA size standard for its NAICS code; the inn's receipts (about $180,000) are far below the $9.0 million standard for NAICS 721191
The inn has no California operations and its revenue is far below the law's thresholds

A controller under Fla. Stat. 501.702 must exceed $1 billion in global gross annual revenue and meet one of three further tests (online advertising revenue, a smart speaker and voice command service, or a large app store); the inn meets none
The inn is not a health plan or health care provider and handles no claims; it is not a covered entity

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule and Red Flags Rule
basis: The inn extends no consumer credit; guests pay by card at booking, check-in or departure
The business is a sole proprietorship and is not publicly traded
The inn holds no federal contracts or subcontracts; its income comes from guest stays

obligation: Payment facilitator sub-merchant agreement: incident notice
basis: Notice to the facilitator within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise

obligation: Card brand compromise rules (Visa; American Express; other brands as the facilitator directs)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0; American Express DSOP Section 3
basis: Card brand rules reach the inn through the sub-merchant agreement; the facilitator coordinates reporting
